races.name: Widmer Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier)

runners_data.name: Doyouknowwhatimean
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner here; Brogan will likely bowl along uncontested from flag to finish, and recent Good-ground form (2W5P in 15 similar-going runs) supports the profile, though the STYLE_FIT flag is a mild caution that the horse doesn't always replicate this role reliably.

runners_data.name: A Little Something
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 2m on Good ground for Emma Lavelle, now stretching to 2m4f for the first time — the extra distance is the key question, but the form reads well and Ben Jones has a positive booking; prominent style maps perfectly to this race shape.

runners_data.name: Greer Hill
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with a recent 2m win on Good ground and handled by a 5lb claimer in Shanahan — the step up from 2m to 2m4f is a genuine query, but the tongue-tie addition and active stable form (2/20 in 14 days) keep this in view.

runners_data.name: Holy Legend
runners_data.note: Won over 2m and 2m2f on Good recently and the hold-up style is genuine; races from the rear naturally and James Best is an able partner, but the 46-day absence and the fact that a steady pace won't fully maximise the finishing kick are the principal concerns.

runners_data.name: Traveling Soldier
runners_data.note: Naturally a hold-up horse — Sean Bowen's mount will be racing closer to the pace than ideal given the crowded rear, and the v-hood and 50-day break add layers of uncertainty; all five recent runs on Good produced no wins, though the form figures show consistent placing.

runners_data.name: King Of The Story
runners_data.note: Experienced ten-year-old with 14 of 15 career runs on Good ground and three wins in that category — prominent style fits this race well, and the t-hood is retained; the recent P4-2P7 form string shows he finds one or two too good but stays in the mix at this level.

runners_data.name: Crackerjack Queen
runners_data.note: Consistent finisher in mid-division; her natural instinct is to race off the pace but she'll find herself unable to get the true hold-up berth in this field — trainer Ellis has two wins from five in 14 days and the mare has course-and-distance placed form, so she's not without a chance if the fractions quicken.

runners_data.name: Boskill Borden
runners_data.note: Returning from a 293-day absence — that alone is the dominant story here; a hold-up horse by nature who will be squeezed into a midfield role he wouldn't naturally seek, and the long layoff means fitness is unproven despite Good-ground familiarity across 13 of 15 career starts.

races.paceDynamic: Doyouknowwhatimean is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner field and, with no genuine rival to push the pace, Kevin Brogan can dictate terms at a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 2m4f trip on Good ground at Worcester. A Little Something and King Of The Story are the most likely to press from a prominent position, but neither has the profile to forcibly take the race away from the leader early. Critically, Traveling Soldier, Crackerjack Queen, and Boskill Borden are all true hold-up horses by nature but are mapped to midfield because the field cannot accommodate that many genuine closers at the rear — their natural late-run style will be compromised by a race that forces them to race closer than ideal. This shape — a lone front-runner setting a steady, uncontested tempo — classically favours horses who can travel prominently and produce a jump-for-jump challenge in the straight, making the prominent-to-lead profile the clear tactical beneficiary.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Doyouknowwhatimean Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Doyouknowwhatimean is allowed to bowl along at his own pace and no rival mounts a sustained early challenge.
scenarios.body: Brogan dictates from the front over an uncontested, even gallop, conserving energy over the fences before quickening in the straight — Good ground suits the horse's recent form profile (2W5P in similar conditions). Prominent chasers who can travel smoothly and attack the final two fences are best positioned, and A Little Something's back-to-back winning form at this trip on identical going makes the profile highly relevant.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Fight Out
scenarios.trigger: If A Little Something or King Of The Story applies sustained pressure to Doyouknowwhatimean from the second circuit, turning it into a battle for the lead.
scenarios.body: The front end becomes a duel that tests both pace-setters, with the winner likely being the one who jumps more fluently and maintains rhythm — A Little Something's consecutive wins at 2m on Good ground and now stepping to 2m4f gives scope, but Holy Legend, fresh from a 2m win, could creep into it late.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Defies Crowd
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to compromise the front two late and one of the redistributed hold-up types finds room to finish powerfully.
scenarios.body: This scenario requires Traveling Soldier, Crackerjack Queen, or Boskill Borden to overcome the positional disadvantage of racing closer than their natural style — a significant ask given their STYLE_FIT discounts and the fact that the pace is unlikely to be fierce enough to make their late run rewarding. Sean Bowen's horsemanship on Traveling Soldier gives this the best chance of the three, but the probability remains low precisely because these horses are not racing in their natural role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Attrition Chase, Survivor Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the jumping errors or early fallers disrupt the field and the race becomes a jumping contest of errors rather than a tactical race.
scenarios.body: In a scrambling, incident-affected race the most experienced and reliable jumper at this level inherits the advantage — King Of The Story's wealth of course-and-distance experience (14/15 runs on Good) and Greer Hill's recent course win at 2m on Good give each a route into the frame.

watchPoints.text: Watch Doyouknowwhatimean at the early fences — if Brogan settles him into an uncontested lead without a jumping error at the first two, the race is likely to be run entirely on his terms and the pace dynamic is set for the remainder.

Monitor A Little Something's jumping on the second circuit — if Ben Jones decides to press for the lead, this becomes a different race shape; if he sits a length off and waits, the extra 4f over her usual 2m trip becomes the decisive test in the straight.

Traveling Soldier, Crackerjack Queen, and Boskill Borden are all true closers racing out of their natural position — if the pace is slow, none will get the run they need and any punter relying on a late surge should be aware these are compromised tactical positions.
Boskill Borden's 293-day absence makes him the biggest fitness unknown in the field — watch his behaviour in the paddock and his jumping at the early fences for signs of a horse that needed the run.

Greer Hill is the only five-year-old and the youngest in the field tackling 2m4f for the first time — how William Shanahan positions him off the pace in the first mile will indicate whether Jennie Candlish has primed him for this step up.

races.name: Land O Plums Clives Of Copthorne Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Mt Fugi Park
runners_data.note: Sole confirmed front-runner who will bowl along in front on his preferred Good ground; form figures show a recent win at Hawthorn Hill over 24f on Good and he's well-handled by the O'Neill yard, though he's racing slightly out of true role here mapping as Prominent — the bigger risk is complacency if unchallenged over this longer 2m7f trip.

runners_data.name: Regal Renaissance
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins heading into this, all at shorter trips than 2m7f, but his Good-going record is outstanding (9/15) and he races with genuine tactical versatility just off the pace; Sean Bowen is a major upgrade in the saddle and the 17-day turnaround under a yard running at 2/17 in the last fortnight gives mild pause.

runners_data.name: Tiger Orchid
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old with a strong hold-up style who has hit the frame or won in four of his last five over similar Going; Charlie Hammond keeps the ride, and his best form — including a win at 24f on Good — aligns well with today's conditions, though he needs the race to develop into a proper stamina test.

runners_data.name: Court In A Storm
runners_data.note: Well-travelled prominent-style chaser who has competed at 26f on Good five times in the last five runs and placed three times; the tongue-tie is retained, trainer Bailey/Nicholls is cold at 0/1 in the 14-day window, and he must settle in a busy midfield cluster rather than getting a soft lead, which is his biggest tactical obstacle today.

runners_data.name: Jaramillo
runners_data.note: 256-day absence is the dominant concern here, and his recent form figures of 3-6-5-6 in shorter 20f Good-ground races suggest he's been operating below the level required; Sam Twiston-Davies is a strong booking on a horse who did win at 21f on Good, but the layoff and lack of form over this trip make him a speculative player in every scenario.

runners_data.name: Harrys Hope
runners_data.note: Consistent place-gatherer who has finished second five times in his last six attempts but cannot find the killer blow; Ben Jones retains the ride for a yard that is 0/4 in the 14-day window, and while his Good-going record is fine, he may need a falsely-run race to claim the lead he lacks the authority to secure outright.

runners_data.name: Gwash
runners_data.note: A 7-year-old hold-up type who has been competing on Good ground in 14 of his last 15 runs — as consistent a going profile as any in the field; Tom Broughton's 3lb claim is a welcome allowance at the weights, though his recent form (7-6-5-3-2) suggests he's creeping closer and this longer 2m7f trip could be the key unlocking his first win in some time.

runners_data.name: Axel Bleue
runners_data.note: Won at 23f on Good ground at this track last time out and holds strong course form, but his natural style is front-running/prominent and he has been redistributed into a midfield berth in this mapping because the field is over-populated with prominent types — his tongue-tie and p-headgear suggest he needs to travel with energy, and being denied his position could blunt his effectiveness.

runners_data.name: Grillon De Monty
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old veteran who has placed twice at 23f on Good in recent outings for Stephen Allen's small yard, and he's run just 12 days ago; his natural game is to race prominently but the congested pace map means he's unlikely to get that position freely, and at OR=102 he faces a stiff ask against better-handicapped rivals without the run of the race.

races.paceDynamic: Mt Fugi Park is the lone confirmed front-runner in this 2m7f chase and, with no genuine rival likely to press for the lead, will dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop across the New course. Behind him, Regal Renaissance, Court In A Storm, and Harrys Hope are all prominent-style horses competing for the same ground, creating a compressed, jostling group in the early-to-mid stages rather than a true two-horse pace duel. The hold-up horses Tiger Orchid, Jaramillo, and Gwash will be settled in behind a relatively steady tempo, meaning the race is likely to be run at a rhythm that suits those coming late — but only if the race doesn't collapse into a sprint at the second-last. The combination of a lone front-runner setting a measured pace over a stamina trip on Good ground most strongly favours prominent horses tracking just off the gallop who can pounce at the third-last, giving Regal Renaissance and Court In A Storm the ideal platform, while genuine hold-up horses will need the pace to quicken to draw them into it. The field carries more prominent types than can all hold their preferred position: Axel Bleue and Grillon De Monty are natural front-of-midfield horses who have been pushed back in the mapping, and Regal Renaissance and Court In A Storm are most likely to secure the prominent berths ahead of them.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Mt Fugi Park dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and prominent trackers hunt him down from the third-last.
scenarios.body: Mt Fugi Park sets the fractions from the front and the race develops into a stamina test over the final half-mile, with the horses tracking him in second and third perfectly placed to strike.
winners: Regal Renaissance runs into his hat-trick in a race shape that suits his front-tracking style on Good ground
is ideally drawn off the pace-setter.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is brisk enough to string the field out and genuine closers have ground to make up turning in.
scenarios.body: A quicker early tempo from Mt Fugi Park — perhaps pushed wider or landing awkwardly — stretches the field and leaves the hold-up types with a clean run up the home straight.
winners: Tiger Orchid's five career wins and strong record on Good going makes this his scenario
a former winner who handles this track and trip
would benefit from a truly-run race.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Scrimmage
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent horses — Regal Renaissance, Court In A Storm, Harrys Hope — races too keenly and burns each other out chasing Mt Fugi Park.
scenarios.body: The early stages become messy as several horses compete for the same ground just behind the leader, costing energy at a critical stage of a 2m7f chase.
winners: who travels prominently but has shown the ability to idle and conserve
while Gwash's recent placed run at 23f on Good shows he handles the trip well enough to pick up the pieces.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Axel Bleue or Grillon De Monty contest for their natural prominent position aggressively and disrupt the pace dynamic.
scenarios.body: Neither horse is truly a hold-up type and if either fights for position it injects an unexpected injection of pace into the first mile, fragmenting the field.
winners: a confirmed winner on Good at 23f
would be benefiting from racing in a natural position rather than a manufactured one; Grillon De Monty's recent second at 23f on Good shows residual ability if conditions suit.

watchPoints.text: Regal Renaissance has won three on the bounce and Sean Bowen takes over the ride — watch whether he slots into second behind Mt Fugi Park before the fourth fence, because if he gets that position the race may already be over.

Court In A Storm, Harrys Hope, and Regal Renaissance are all prominent types converging on the same ground in the early stages — a jostling match approaching the third fence could see one lose position or be hampered, fundamentally altering each horse's race shape.

Jaramillo has been off 256 days and jumps fences for the first time after a run of flat-style hurdle-pace form at 20f — watch how sharp he is at the first two obstacles, as any blunder from a horse returning from that long a layoff can disrupt horses immediately behind him.

Mt Fugi Park set to lead unchallenged, but on 2m7f Good ground at Worcester the pace can drop dramatically on the long run to the home straight — if the leader crawls, hold-up horses like Tiger Orchid and Gwash may find themselves with nothing to aim at turning in.

Axel Bleue and Grillon De Monty both hold prominent profiles but have been mapped to midfield by necessity — watch whether either forces the issue from the start, because an unexpected injection of early pace from either would reframe the entire tactical picture.

races.name: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle Race (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race) (Div I)

runners_data.name: Arcon
runners_data.note: Trained by Jennie Candlish, showed a placed effort in good going over 14f and carries a tongue tie; a genuine hold-up horse by nature, displaced forward on the map to midfield — the redistribution means it won't get the deep closing position where it does its best work, and the STYLE_FIT flag tempers confidence here.

runners_data.name: Devon Red
runners_data.note: 782 days off the track makes this a significant unknown quantity; Quinlan takes the mount for Nick Scholfield, going is not a concern but race-fitness after such a long absence is the dominant question mark.

runners_data.name: Military Saint
runners_data.note: Tom Bellamy rides this David Dennis horse who has one good-ground hurdle run to his name and a win in that sim-going reference; unknown style but the positive form line gives him a live each-way chance in a tactical race.

runners_data.name: Not Now
runners_data.note: Sam Twiston-Davies partners this hold-up type for the family yard; has placed in good ground twice over 16-17f and should appreciate the 2m trip, though needs the pace to set up a late run — a measured gallop makes things harder.

runners_data.name: Trackman
runners_data.note: David Noonan rides; consistent hold-up performer who has finished in the 5-6 range on good ground multiple times without threatening; needs strong pace to get competitive, which this race shape is unlikely to generate.

runners_data.name: Delgany Second Now
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's 4yo has gone 7-7 in recent starts on good ground; a natural closer whose true rear position is crowded out by rivals, so Tristan Durrell will be forced further forward than ideal — the style fit discount applies.

runners_data.name: Faithful Guardian
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's 4yo has two placed efforts at 16f on good ground, suggesting this trip and surface are in his comfort zone; Theo Gillard rides, and as a horse who appears to travel prominently, he is well positioned to exploit a controlled gallop set by the Skelton stablemate.

runners_data.name: Iwanttobreakfree
runners_data.note: The race pivot — Harry Skelton's assured front-running tactics for Dan Skelton make this horse the architect of the race shape; two runs into its career with a place on good ground and tongue tie noted, the big question is whether it can jump well enough under pressure to hold on.

runners_data.name: Provision
runners_data.note: F Brennan's 4yo has three placed efforts at 16f on good ground and clearly goes on the surface; Isabelle Ryder (5lb claim) rides, but as a true hold-up type bumped forward into midfield on the map, the structural disadvantage in this steady-pace shape is real.

runners_data.name: Galeforcechopper
runners_data.note: James Turner (5lb) takes the ride for David Brace; hg flag (hood/tongue tie combo) and three runs on good ground including a place at 17f suggests the trip is fine, but a hold-up profile and modest form figures make it hard to see a winning scenario without a complete pace collapse.

races.paceDynamic: Iwanttobreakfree is the sole confirmed front-runner and, ridden by Harry Skelton for Dan Skelton, will stride straight to the front and control tempo from the outset over this 2m trip at Worcester. With no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, the pace will be measured and sustainable — Skelton can dictate, conserve energy over hurdles, and quicken when he chooses approaching the final flight. This race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently or within a length or two of the leader, as the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to set up a late finish for genuine hold-up horses. The field carries more hold-up intent than the map can accommodate: Arcon, Delgany Second Now, and Provision are natural closers redistributed to midfield, meaning they are unlikely to secure the rearmost ground they need to produce their best, further tilting the advantage toward the front-running and prominent profile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Iwanttobreakfree Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Iwanttobreakfree meets no pace pressure and dictates a steady, front-running race at a tempo entirely of Harry Skelton's choosing.
scenarios.body: Iwanttobreakfree rolls along uncontested, jumps fluently, and has enough left to quicken away from the final hurdle before rivals can mount a sustained challenge; horses close enough in midfield are the only realistic threat.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Chase Home
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is steady enough that horses racing just off Iwanttobreakfree can track and pounce in the straight.
scenarios.body: Faithful Guardian and Military Saint, both likely to settle in second or third, have the fitness and going form to land a challenge as the field fans out; the controlled pace suits horses who can switch off and finish strongly rather than make it from the front.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Gets Up
scenarios.trigger: If the pace stalls sharply in the final mile and one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to secure a forward enough berth to be competitive.
scenarios.body: Arcon or Delgany Second Now, both mapped to midfield rather than their natural rear position, would need a genuine pace collapse to pick up enough momentum to challenge; this scenario is structurally weaker because neither horse is racing in its true role.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Capitulates
scenarios.trigger: If Iwanttobreakfree sets a pace that proves too aggressive for its jumping ability and weakens after the third-last hurdle.
scenarios.body: A horse like Not Now or Galeforcechopper, travelling smoothly in the chasing pack, inherits the lead on a tiring Iwanttobreakfree and holds on; this scenario requires a jumping error or stamina failure from the leader, which is possible but against the weight of evidence.

watchPoints.text: Iwanttobreakfree jumping — any mistake at a hurdle with Harry Skelton in full control of the race tempo could unravel the dominant scenario and hand the initiative to the chasing pack immediately.

Faithful Guardian's positioning at the start — if Theo Gillard slots him directly onto Iwanttobreakfree's heels, he is arguably the biggest threat to the leader and the race could become a two-horse duel from halfway.
Devon Red's race-fitness after 782 days absent is completely untested; if it misses the break or is outpaced early, it could cause interference from the rear and disrupt horses mapped to midfield.

The redistribution cluster of Arcon, Delgany Second Now, and Provision all competing for the same midfield ground creates a risk of crowding at the first hurdle — watch for early traffic problems among this group as none is racing in its natural position.

Military Saint's unknown style profile means Tom Bellamy could place him almost anywhere — if he elects to ride prominently off the pace, he becomes a live danger who is currently underweighted in most scenarios.

races.name: Colin Jones Memorial Maiden Hurdle Race (ARC Summer Novices' Brush Hurdle Series Qualifier) (GBB Race) (Div II)

runners_data.name: Happy Chandler
runners_data.note: Has winning form on Good ground and a solid recent record, suits a prominent-to-midfield tracking role that puts him in the right position if the pace set by Without Burlington proves honest; Harry Reed keeps it straightforward and 39 days off is no concern.|

runners_data.name: Lucky Diamond
runners_data.note: Dropped in trip from 16f+ hurdles and has an unseat in recent form, the step back to 2m on Good ground is an unknown quantity; Liam Harrison will need to manage a horse whose style is uncertain (marked U) and recent form figures offer little confidence.|

runners_data.name: Penzance
runners_data.note: John Joseph Hanlon's 6-year-old shows a decent placed record on Good ground, but is a natural hold-up horse operating here closer to the pace than he would like due to the abundance of closers in the field; his chance is real if the tempo quickens but the positional compromise is genuine.|

runners_data.name: Starshine Legend
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's 5-year-old has a T14 win on the board and showed a placed effort over 16f, stepping back to 2m with Sean Bowen — one of the best tactical jockeys in the race — could allow him to find a better position than his usual hold-up tag implies.|

runners_data.name: Bound For Glory
runners_data.note: Ciaran Gethings rides a horse with a recent win on Good ground over 16f and two placed efforts to his name; prominent style suits this race shape perfectly as the only horse likely to sit directly behind or alongside Without Burlington, giving him a clear line of sight at the leader.|

runners_data.name: Delgany Headline
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton's 4-year-old returns from 136 days off after a single run — a poor eighth on Soft — and the form flag for fading in the finish is a red light in a race where hold-up types are already compromised; the lengthy break combined with minimal form makes this a speculative entry.|

runners_data.name: Earnest Belief
runners_data.note: Donald McCain's 4-year-old has been remarkably consistent without winning, placing in five of his last seven, but is a natural hold-up horse squeezed into a midfield role here; the tongue-tie is retained, and while Theo Gillard is capable, the positional issue is the primary obstacle to a bold show.|

runners_data.name: Without Burlington
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. takes the ride on a horse who won his last two on flat on Good and Standard, but 289 days off is a significant fitness question mark heading this race on the front end; the STYLE_FIT tag is applied because he will be making the running from a prominent-mapped position, and if the layoff tells in the final half-mile the race turns on its head.|

races.paceDynamic: Without Burlington is the sole confirmed front-runner and, coming back from 289 days off, will set a controlled, uncontested gallop that allows Jonjo O'Neill Jr. to dictate every yard of the pace on his own terms — this is a genuinely sustainable lead with no realistic challenger for the front. Bound For Glory is the only other horse with a prominent style and will sit second or third, meaning the race is run at a tempo shaped entirely by Without Burlington's stamina and fitness level. The field contains more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear — Delgany Headline, Penzance, and Earnest Belief are genuine hold-up horses shuffled into midfield positions they won't naturally occupy, which compresses the back of the field and limits their ability to produce their usual late run. This race shape — a single unhurried front-runner setting a steady pace — overwhelmingly favours horses who can sit prominently or just off the pace and accelerate in the straight, with true hold-up finishers disadvantaged by the likely lack of early tempo to exploit.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Without Burlington sets an uncontested, measured gallop and the pace proves sustainable enough to reward those tracking close.
scenarios.body: Without Burlington dictates from the front with Bound For Glory in attendance, and the race is run at a rhythm that suits those close enough to pounce in the final half-mile; horses unable to get into a challenging position early are left with too much ground to make up on Good going.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Stops, Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Without Burlington's long absence (289 days) takes its toll late and the horse weakens approaching the final hurdle.
scenarios.body: Bound For Glory, travelling prominently throughout, inherits the lead and has the fitness edge of a recent run to sustain the effort; horses who have been tracking midfield with cover, like Happy Chandler, are best placed to capitalise if the prominent duo tire.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Midfield Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Without Burlington sets a sharper-than-expected pace that strings the field out and creates genuine gaps for midfield movers.
scenarios.body: Horses like Happy Chandler, who has winning form on this going and enough tactical speed to advance from off the pace, find themselves in the right position as the front comes back to the field; Starshine Legend, with Sean Bowen navigating from midfield, could also pick up the pieces if the pace collapse is significant.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If Without Burlington goes off too fast and the pace collapses dramatically, giving true closers an unusually long run to the line.
scenarios.body: Penzance and Earnest Belief are genuine hold-up horses forced into midfield, meaning their chance depends on a pace scenario that rarely materialises with a single front-runner in a maiden hurdle; even if the setup were right, their redistribution out of their natural position reduces the likelihood they execute their finishing run effectively.

watchPoints.text: Without Burlington's 289-day absence is the pivotal unknown — watch his jumping and body language in the early stages; if he starts to labour at the third-last hurdle Bound For Glory is ideally placed to inherit.|

Delgany Headline returns from 136 days off with a single poor run to his name and a known tendency to fade — watch whether he travels with any fluency or is struggling to keep tabs as early as halfway.|

Majestic Leo has pulled up in his last two hurdle starts and carries a fade-in-finish flag; if he begins to lose his action or jump sloppily in the back straight, Isabelle Ryder should not be persisted with.|

Bound For Glory's prominent style is perfectly aligned with this race shape — watch whether Ciaran Gethings elects to sit on Without Burlington's quarters from the outset or gives him a length or two of rope, as that positioning decision will shape the entire finishing order.|

The trio of redistributed hold-up horses — Penzance, Earnest Belief, and Delgany Headline — will be unable to drop out as far as they ideally want; watch the early gallop to see if any of them get badly crowded or lose their rhythm through the first two flights.|

races.name: Dolphin Tec Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: T Or Coffey
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with strong similar-going form (1W3P on Good/Standard) and a course-and-distance win last season; returning from 238 days off is the key query, though Jennie Candlish's 2/20 T14 suggests the yard is in modest form — tongue tie applied, and Lewis Stones' 3lb claim helps offset the fitness doubt.

runners_data.name: Break Point
runners_data.note: Ran just 16 days ago and finished third over 18f on Good, bringing sharpness into this; natural hold-up horse who has won at this trip, and Kielan Woods rides well off the pace — the 10/20f run on Good (10th) hints at this 2m as his preferred stamina ceiling rather than beyond.

runners_data.name: Media Mogul
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this course and distance on Good, making him the one confirmed front-runner in the field; Tom Dascombe's yard is 0/8 in the T14 window which is a mild flag, but David Bass can dictate terms from the front and the 35-day freshener suits — the sim-going profile (2W4P in 14 runs) is solid.

runners_data.name: Tilehurst
runners_data.note: Consistent placed performer on Good ground with five consecutive runs over 2m at this track producing finishes of 5-4-2-3-3; Sean Bowen is a major upgrade in the saddle and tongue tie worn — prominent style suits the likely race shape but has not won since going eligible, and the placed-but-not-winning pattern is a concern.

runners_data.name: Kernie d'Airy
runners_data.note: Won last time over this exact course and distance on Good, giving him a live claims; Jamie Snowden's yard is 2/10 in the T14 window and Gavin Sheehan is a strong booking — sim-going figures are a modest 3/4 but that sample is small and the course form is the standout angle here.

runners_data.name: Ez Tiger
runners_data.note: A genuinely prominent-racing type that has been pushed into the midfield slot because this field cannot accommodate all its front-runners — his 11/15 sim-going record (3W7P) is the best in the race and he is capable of winning, but racing out of role on a track where position matters carries a real cost (STYLE_FIT 0.91).

runners_data.name: Playful Fox
runners_data.note: Harry Skelton takes a significant booking for a horse that won last time over this course and distance on Good; in truth a natural front-runner who cannot get his head in front early given Media Mogul's presence, so Dan Skelton's four-year-old must do it the hard way from a position he does not naturally occupy — the 156lb burden is the lightest in the race and he is hurdling experience-light at age 4.

races.paceDynamic: Media Mogul is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, David Bass can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 2m trip on Good ground at Worcester. The field contains more prominent-minded horses than can all secure their preferred position — Playful Fox and Ez Tiger are both natural front-runners who will be shuffled into midfield roles against their instincts, creating a compressed mid-pack rather than genuine pressure on Media Mogul. With a single, uncontested pace-setter likely to bowl along at a measured clip, this race sets up as a test of staying power over the final two flights rather than a gruelling slog, and horses capable of travelling smoothly just off the lead and producing a clean jump at the last will be best placed. This shape firmly favours hold-up and prominent horses that can close off a genuine gallop — T Or Coffey and Break Point, both natural hold-up types with strong sim-going profiles, are ideally positioned to exploit a race run to suit their style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Media Mogul Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Media Mogul bowls along at a comfortable solo gallop and the pace-pressers Playful Fox and Ez Tiger settle for midfield slots without burning early energy.
scenarios.body: Media Mogul dictates a measured pace, jumps fluently, and Bass extends the advantage from two out with no one able to accelerate past him; the hold-up horses face too much ground to make up on a horse that has never been tested. Prominent horses with clean jumping and stamina to match the front-runner's reserves benefit most from this controlled shape.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Surge Late
scenarios.trigger: If Media Mogul's gallop is just strong enough to drain the prominent horses and the genuine closers find a clear run from two out.
scenarios.body: T Or Coffey and Break Point, both proven in similar going and over this trip, close off a true-enough pace set by Media Mogul and arrive late with momentum the front-runner cannot match; Lewis Stones' claim and T Or Coffey's course-proven sim-going figures (1W3P) make this a live threat. Break Point's recent run just 16 days ago keeps him sharp and Kielan Woods can deliver from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Unfolds
scenarios.trigger: If Playful Fox or Ez Tiger refuse to settle and contest the early gallop with Media Mogul, injecting genuine pace and unsettling the field.
scenarios.body: A contested lead inflates the gallop, the mid-division compresses as pace-pressers scramble for position, and the resulting test suits a horse that relaxes and travels — Kernie d'Airy, who won last time over this course and trip on Good, is well placed with Gavin Sheehan. Tilehurst's consistent placed form on Good ground also brings him into play if the front runners tie each other up.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Types Capitalise
scenarios.trigger: If both redistributed prominent types (Playful Fox, Ez Tiger) are hampered or make errors that bring them back into the pack, gifting cover to midfield horses.
scenarios.body: Ez Tiger's 11/15 sim-going strike rate is the strongest in the field and if he gets a clear passage despite being out of position, his raw class could overpower a moderate pace; Playful Fox, the youngest in the field at age 4, could also outrun his disadvantaged map position with natural athleticism and Harry Skelton's tactical brilliance. However, both horses carry STYLE_FIT discounts and this remains the least likely shape given their unnatural placement.

watchPoints.text: Media Mogul's jumping is the fulcrum of this race — if David Bass gets fluent leaps at every hurdle with no pressure, he can sustain the advantage all the way to the line; a mistake at a late flight is the only thing that can bring him back.

Playful Fox and Ez Tiger are both wired to race prominently and may instinctively chase Media Mogul regardless of their connections' intentions — if either commits early, the pace lifts sharply and the hold-up horses' closing scenario becomes significantly more viable.

T Or Coffey is 238 days off the track, and while the yard has placed runners in similar scenarios, first-run fitness in a competitive handicap hurdle on Good ground is a live concern that could prevent the horse from landing its finishing effort at a crucial moment.

Tilehurst has produced five consecutive placed efforts at this track on Good ground but has not won; watch whether Sean Bowen attempts to track Media Mogul more aggressively than previous jockeys, as a change in tactics from this consistent type could be the difference between another place and a first win.

Kernie d'Airy's recent course-and-distance win makes him the most direct form threat to Media Mogul in similar conditions — watch the market for any support as Sheehan plots a hold-up ride to arrive late against the clear front-runner.

races.name: Bathroom Studio Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Roadshow
runners_data.note: The sole natural front-runner here; Paul Nicholls in good recent form (T14 1/1) and Keighley's 5lb claim adds value, though STYLE_FIT of 0.93 flags he is stepping outside his absolute comfort zone — his recent good-ground form over similar trips is solid and the uncontested lead is the key asset.

runners_data.name: Blue Universe
runners_data.note: Paddy Hanlon's amateur claim is an asset in a handicap, but 89 days off and a pulled-up last start on good ground raises fitness questions; a genuine hold-up type who needs a stronger pace than Roadshow is likely to set to finish off his race.

runners_data.name: Little Ledgend
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen is a major jockey booking for a horse who has been consistently placed (four seconds in last five starts); suited by good ground and looks set to race prominently off the pace — the biggest danger to Roadshow in a tracking role.

runners_data.name: Achille Des Rocs
runners_data.note: Pulled up twice since a course win but has a 2W2P record on similar good ground; prominent style should allow him to travel in a good position, though his jumping and consistency under pressure are the chief concerns with a 43-day absence.

runners_data.name: Estacas
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old who has shown recent good-ground form with a place at 20f, handled by a 3lb claimer Luke Scott; naturally a hold-up type but will likely end up closer than ideal given the overcrowded rear, which may not play to his strengths.

runners_data.name: Midnight Jewel
runners_data.note: 277 days off the track is a massive fitness flag for a 10-year-old; has good-ground form at the trip and two wins on similar going in history, but the layoff makes it very hard to trust at any price.

runners_data.name: The Grayster
runners_data.note: Only four years old in a field of veterans and just three runs over hurdles; Harry Skelton is an elite booking and gives the gelding every chance, but 167 days off and limited form base on soft make his good-ground claims uncertain.

runners_data.name: Bashful Boy
runners_data.note: David Pipe's ten-year-old was last seen finishing third 12 days ago, so racecourse freshness is fine; a natural hold-up horse who will be dragged closer than he wants in this field, making it hard for him to produce his characteristic late finish.

runners_data.name: Pivotal Days
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with modest recent form figures (4-9-6) and ridden by a 5lb claimer; runs naturally from off the pace but is shunted into midfield on the map — still finds itself out of role regardless, and the form profile does not inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: The Padster
runners_data.note: Showed a career-best effort last time (2nd, 20f, good) and clearly handles the trip; Callum Pritchard takes the ride but the horse is a true hold-up type who will struggle to recapture that finishing position if forced to race closer than preferred.

runners_data.name: Medina Blue
runners_data.note: Five-year-old with form figures of 2-2 earlier in his career but recent runs showing 6-7-7; four runs on similar good ground with no win, ridden by 3lb claimer Joe Anderson — naturally sits deep and the congested hold-up section complicates matters.

runners_data.name: Quick Of The Night
runners_data.note: Consistent horse with five placings in last five on good ground; front-to-midfield style is well suited to tracking the leader and a good-ground course specialist record (13/15 on similar going) makes him a reliable each-way contender in this shape.

runners_data.name: Gone In Sixty
runners_data.note: Alex Hales' nine-year-old ran second last time at 20f on good and brings strong course-and-distance profile (14/15 on similar going); prominent style suits the race shape and Kielan Woods is a capable partner, though his OR has drifted down a long way.

races.paceDynamic: Roadshow is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 13-runner handicap hurdle and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Freddie Keighley can dictate at a controlled, sustainable gallop over the 2m4f trip on good ground at Worcester. Little Ledgend, Achille Des Rocs, Quick Of The Night and Gone In Sixty are all prominent-style types who will contest the early positions behind Roadshow, creating a competitive but measured pace rather than a true test of stamina. The field carries a significant hold-up population — Bashful Boy, Pivotal Days, The Padster and Medina Blue are all genuine hold-up horses redistributed toward midfield on the map because there is no room at the rear for all of them, meaning they will be racing closer than their natural style. With one dictating front-runner setting an unforced tempo, this race shape strongly favours horses who can race prominently and travel into the race at relatively little cost — particularly those with tactical pace to press the leader from the second flight and produce a sharp finish at the business end.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Roadshow Controls And Holds
scenarios.trigger: If Roadshow is allowed to bowl along uncontested at a fair but manageable gallop and the prominent chasers cannot reel him in.
scenarios.body: Freddie Keighley dictates every yard from the front, the pace is honest enough to keep hold-up horses honest but not fast enough to burn out Roadshow's stamina, and the 5yo rounds the final turn with a healthy lead; horses who tracked him prominently — Little Ledgend, Quick Of The Night — are best placed to mount a challenge but may simply be outgunned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Racer Reels Him In
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just quick enough that Roadshow ties up approaching the last and a prominent tracker swoops past.
scenarios.body: Little Ledgend or Gone In Sixty, travelling within themselves in the first half, improve to press Roadshow from three out and use superior fresh reserves to wear down the leader at the final hurdle; this suits horses with a high recent finishing record who can sustain a long run from the top of the straight.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Picks Up Late
scenarios.trigger: If the gallop is genuinely strong enough that prominent types empty out, allowing a midfield runner to emerge from the pack late.
scenarios.body: Estacas or Blue Universe, who have genuine hold-up credentials and course-distance track records on good ground, close from mid-division through a weakening pack; however, with most true hold-up horses displaced toward midfield rather than their natural deep position, this scenario requires an unusually fast early pace that the race shape does not readily support.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Scrambles The Result
scenarios.trigger: If jumping errors, interference or a collapse in the pace in the final mile produces a muddled finish with unexpected positional changes.
scenarios.body: A horse that has been squeezed out of its natural position — such as Bashful Boy or The Padster, both running closer than ideal — might stumble into contention through attrition rather than merit; this is the least likely shape given the uncomplicated pace picture and the presence of multiple prominent types to keep the tempo honest.

watchPoints.text: Roadshow's uncontested lead is the key race-shaping factor — watch whether Freddie Keighley elects to dominate immediately from the gate or is pushed wide early by the prominent pack, as any disruption to his front-running role significantly changes the outcome.

Little Ledgend's consistency (four seconds in five) allied with Sean Bowen's tactical intelligence makes her the primary player if Roadshow's lead is reeled in — watch how Bowen positions her relative to the front-runner through the back straight.

The Grayster carries Harry Skelton's 4-year-old booking at just three runs in; a layoff of 167 days on unfamiliar ground means watch the betting market for any late support as a potential dark horse for the Skelton yard.

Midnight Jewel returns from 277 days off — watch paddock condition closely before the race, as any sign of a light or unready appearance should significantly downgrade her chances despite a strong historical record on this going.

Blue Universe, Bashful Boy, Pivotal Days and The Padster are all genuine hold-up horses forced to race closer than natural — if the pace collapses in the back straight and they bunch up in midfield, watch for jumping errors or interference that could unseat or hamper multiple runners simultaneously.

races.name: PJ Nicholls KGM Korea Genuinely Made Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Roxboro River
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up performer for John Joseph Hanlon, ran only 4 days ago which is a significant freshness flag; that rapid turnaround may blunt effectiveness, though sim-going record of 15/15 on Good with 1 win and 3 placings is excellent and the 2m7f trip suits her style.

runners_data.name: Back To Cali
runners_data.note: Dan Skelton in strong 14-day form (6/25), Harry Skelton takes the ride; confirmed front-runner who gets an uncontested lead here but is tagged style-fit 0.92 meaning she is racing slightly outside her sharpest conditions — controls this race but stamina at the extreme end of this trip is the key question.

runners_data.name: Catuaba
runners_data.note: Returning from 652 days off for Charlie Longsdon — a massive absence flag — but has a strong stamina profile (2 wins at 25-26f on Good) and wears a hood; if fit enough, prominent style suits this shape well, but the layoff is a serious concern.

runners_data.name: Barry Fife
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up type for Sam Twiston-Davies carrying a hood; ran 21 days ago with a moderate recent form string including a pulled-up run, and Good ground sim-record of 4/7 is modest — needs a strongly run race to deliver his hold-up challenge.

runners_data.name: Lunar Morning
runners_data.note: Unquantified style for Max Comley, visor fitted; form includes a pulled-up run and recent finishes of 5th and 3rd at similar trips on Good — moderate claim and distance suitability is untested beyond 23f, so the 2m7f here represents a step up in trip.

runners_data.name: Spitalfield
runners_data.note: Patient hold-up type for Jonjo O'Neill Jr. who has been placed in 3 of last 5 on Good; trainer in solid 14-day form (3/14) and 12 days since last run is fine — needs a truly contested gallop to land a blow from off the pace.

runners_data.name: Indian Sunbird
runners_data.note: Strong claims on paper — 3 wins and 6 placings from 15 Good-ground runs, prominent style fits the projected race shape perfectly, and Harry Bannister takes a nice book — the 17-day absence is ideal and the 2m7f trip suits a confirmed stayer.

runners_data.name: Swingforthefence
runners_data.note: 112 days off the track for Jennie Candlish (2/20 in 14-day window), wears tongue-tie and pads; form string of 79768 is deeply uninspiring, sim-going record thin, and the extended absence combined with modest form makes this a speculative runner.

runners_data.name: Mancero
runners_data.note: Young 4-year-old for David Pipe running prominently; all five recent runs have been at 20f so the step to 2m7f is a significant trip query — wears a hood and has a respectable sim-going mark, but whether the stamina stretches this far is genuinely unresolved.

runners_data.name: Luminaries
runners_data.note: Consistent bottom-of-the-market performer for Ewan Whillans; OR=79 in a field rated to 100 represents a significant class gap, recent form includes pulled-up and 9ths, and the tongue-tie/pad headgear combination suggests connections are searching for answers.

runners_data.name: Alderley Charlie
runners_data.note: Moderate recent form with a warning that this horse fades in finishes; in practice a true hold-up type running closer than natural because of the prominent cluster ahead — the style-fit tag (0.90) and that fade tendency make this difficult to fancy even if the trip is appropriate.

runners_data.name: Citizen Jane
runners_data.note: Two recent wins on her form string are encouraging but all five last runs are at shorter trips (16-22f), raising a genuine stamina question over 2m7f; another true hold-up type compressed forward in the field shape, and the 3-claim jockey Charlie Maggs adds further uncertainty.

races.paceDynamic: Back To Cali is the confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, Harry Skelton will be able to dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 2m7f trip on Good ground — a shape that rewards jumping fluency and stamina rather than raw finishing speed. Catuaba, Indian Sunbird, and Mancero are all prominent types who will press for position behind the leader, creating a compact early order but not a breakneck pace that blows the race apart. The field contains more hold-up horses than the race map can accommodate at the rear: Alderley Charlie and Citizen Jane are genuine hold-up types in form but have been redistributed to midfield because the cluster of prominent runners ahead of them will compress the field, forcing them to race closer than ideal. At 2m7f on a fair pace, this race shape strongly favours prominent, front-running profiles with sound jumping and proven stamina on Good ground — horses that can travel on the bridle without being buried in a slowly-run affair and who will not need a dramatic finishing burst.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If Back To Cali sets a fair but uncontested gallop and the race becomes a test of jumping accuracy and staying power from the front.
scenarios.body: Back To Cali controls fractions throughout, the field strings out in the straight, and horses with proven stamina at this trip on Good ground come to the fore; prominent types who travel smoothly into contention are best placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Quickens
scenarios.trigger: If the cluster of prominent types — Catuaba, Mancero, Indian Sunbird — push the pace and the race develops a stronger tempo than Back To Cali intended.
scenarios.body: A more searching gallop tests the field's stamina reserves earlier, eliminating hold-up types who cannot quicken and putting a premium on prominent horses with high RPRs and good form on Good ground.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Delivery Wins
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses to a crawl and the race turns into a sprint finish, allowing mid-division horses to storm through.
scenarios.body: A falsely run race condenses the field and rewards horses who can produce a turn of foot from midfield; Spitalfield and Barry Fife, who track patiently, are best placed to benefit from a late surge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race is truly truly run at a strong gallop from tape to finish and front-runners tie up, gifting late momentum to genuine hold-up types.
scenarios.body: Alderley Charlie and Citizen Jane would theoretically benefit but both are racing closer than their natural style due to redistribution, making this scenario structurally less reliable; Roxboro River, the most genuine hold-up type here on good form, is the most credible late beneficiary.

watchPoints.text: Back To Cali has an uncontested lead but her style-fit tag (0.92) and the step to 2m7f on Good are genuine concerns — watch whether Harry Skelton bowls along or deliberately drops the pace, as either tactic reshapes the entire race.

Catuaba's 652-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race — if Charlie Longsdon has her fit she is a major player given her stamina profile, but a blow-up after a long layoff would reshape the prominent pack significantly.

Mancero's trip stamina is unproven — all his recent runs are at 20f and this is 2m7f; if Sean Bowen tracks up prominently and the horse runs out of gas early it could interfere with other horses in the mid-to-front group.

Alderley Charlie is flagged as fading in finishes and is racing closer than her natural style due to field compression — if she weakens in the straight she could cause jumping problems for horses tracking from midfield behind her.

Roxboro River ran just 4 days ago; monitor in the pre-race paddock for any signs of tiredness — if fresh enough she is the most credible hold-up threat, but rapid turnarounds in staying hurdles frequently catch horses out.
